# Sizing a power station for a fridge

You need to check three numbers: surge watts, continuous watts and watt-hours (Wh).

1. **Surge watts: at least 1,300 W.** This is the number that most often disqualifies a unit. The compressor briefly draws about 2-3x its running watts at startup, commonly 1,000-2,400 W on a household fridge ([BlackBox Supplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage), [HomeGrid HQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/)). Look for a pure sine wave inverter.
2. **Continuous watts: about 250 W or more.** A full-size fridge runs at roughly 100-250 W, so almost any 1,000 W-class station covers this. Add up anything else you'll run at the same time.
3. **Watt-hours: depends on outage length.**
   - **About 1,000 Wh** runs a fridge for roughly 17 hours ([HomeGrid HQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/)).
   - **About 1,400 Wh** covers 24 hours, including inverter losses and headroom.
   - **About 2,800 Wh** covers two days ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator)).

The compressor only runs about 30-40% of the time, so a fridge averages far less than its running watts.

To size for your own fridge, check its EnergyGuide label: kWh per year × 1,000 ÷ 8,760 gives average watts. Large side-by-sides with ice makers can use twice the typical figure. Keeping the door shut helps a lot.

## Options that fit

Prices below are from Dealectric, which tested the codes in each brand's cart on Oct 21-25. Checkout has the final say.

**For most of a day (about 1,000-1,150 Wh):**
- [BLUETTI AC180](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180): 1,152 Wh, 1,800 W, 2,700 W peak. $499, or $474.05 with code AFF5OFF.
- [ALLPOWERS P1800](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-p1800-1024wh): 1,024 Wh, 1,800 W. $439, or $395.10 with code ALLPOWERS26. This is borderline for a full 24 hours, so keep the door closed.

**For a full 24 hours (about 1,400-1,500 Wh):**
- [ALLPOWERS S2000 Pro](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-s2000-pro-1451wh): 1,451 Wh, 2,400 W, and a listed 4,000 W surge. $664, or $597.60 with code ALLPOWERS26. It's right at the 24-hour line, so it leaves little margin for a hot kitchen.

**For two days or more:**
- [BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2): 2,073.6 Wh. $899, or $854.05 with AFF5OFF. Roughly 33 hours by HomeGrid's math.
- [ALLPOWERS R4000](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-r4000-3456wh): 3,456 Wh, 3,600 W. $1,499, or $1,319.12 with EXTRA12. Roughly two days or more.

**Skip the small ones.** A 299 Wh unit like the ALLPOWERS R600 only runs a fridge for about 5 hours, and compact units often can't handle the startup surge.

If you'll run other things too, such as a router, lights or a CPAP, add their draw to the totals. If an outage could last several days, a solar panel helps. ALLPOWERS offers a [P1800 + 400 W solar kit](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-p1800-sp037-solar-kit).

Dealectric's links are affiliate links, so it earns a commission if you buy, at no extra cost to you. Anker's [SOLIX S2000](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/portable-power-station-for-refrigerator) is another option in the 2 kWh class if you'd like to compare.

If you tell me your fridge's size or EnergyGuide kWh/year and how long an outage you want to cover, I can narrow this to one pick.
